title: Organize Your Poms In Clo | Clo Feature Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our POM feature in CLO 2024.2 allows you to organize your POMs into folders and easily show or hide specific grading sizes. Check out other new features here: https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord-

summary: ```markdown # Organize Your POMs In CLO | CLO Feature Deep Dive ## Introduction Hi, my name is Phoebe, and I have some great updates to our POMs, or points of measure. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Overview of Points of Measure (POMs) Here on my screen, I've got some points of measure on my garment, or POMs. If I look over here to my object browser, I'll see all of my points of measure. What's even better is that I'll see a very organized structure of points of measure due to this update with folders. ## Introducing Folders for POMs We also have folders in our fabric section, and we've added them now to our POM tab or points of measure. You can easily add folders through the icon labeled "Create New Folder." When you do that, it will create a whole folder for you where you can house all of those POMs that work within that folder name. ### Adding and Organizing POMs 1. Type in the folder name, for example, "New." 2. You can add points of measure directly underneath that folder by clicking the "Add" button. 3. Additionally, you can click and drag POMs to different folders using a simple drag-and-drop method. ### Managing Folder Contents Right now, I've noticed some discrepancies with my numbering, so I'm just going to click on my number here and change it. When you have a folder in your points of measure, you have a few other options: - **Minimize Folders**: You can minimize your folders by hitting the little arrow, which will collapse it. - **Show All Measurements**: To show everything, you can select the folder again. - **Delete Options**: If you hit the delete button, you'll have two options: - Move all points of measure within the folder to your first folder. - Delete them altogether. I’m going to hit delete, which will remove everything, including the folder itself. However, you can always create another one if you wish. ## Grading Measurements What you can also see here is the grading option at the top. If you've applied grading to your garment, you'll then be able to see all of that measurement. You can hide it if you want by hitting the eye icon, which will hide those graded sizes. I’ll keep these visible for now. ## Adding New Points of Measure Now, I’m going to add another point of measure to my garment. If you prep a bit, you can easily set up all of your folders, add in all of your points of measure, and then go through and add those measurements to your garment. ### Step-by-Step to Add a Point of Measure 1. Hit the "Add" button. 2. Enter the point of measure, for example, "Armhole." 3. Clone knows that the measurement I create here should populate within this point of measure. 4. Click the start and end points for everything and then hit enter when done. ## Editing Points of Measure Next, I'm going to use my edit point of measure tool. Here, I can select these measurements, right-click, and choose "Show Length" to see a complete armhole measurement. If I want a curve measurement instead of a straight one, I can right-click and change the segment type to curve. This will show me the curve measurement for all my graded sizes. ## Viewing 3D and 2D Measurements When I look at all of this, I can also see both my 3D garment measurement and my pattern measurement. This was released in a previous update, but just as a reminder, you can click "3D Line" to show all 3D measurements. Unchecking this will display only my 2D measurement or pattern measurement. ### Comparing Measurements I can always compare these by unchecking the 3D option, which will show only the 2D measurement and the length difference between the garment measurement and the pattern measurement. For example, I see a difference of 1.344 between the pattern and what it is sitting on my garment. ## Saving Your Work One of the last things I want to touch on is how to save all of this. You can easily save by hitting the save button. You can decide whether you want to save your 2D, 3D, or both 2D and 3D lines. ### Importing Measurements Additionally, you can open your POM and save any Excel file or CSV file format into CLO. It will automatically populate all of those measurement names, and you can then go through and add them from your garment. This is what it looks like when you save it. You can see it even keeps it in groups and includes both 2D and 3D measurements. ## Conclusion Thank you so much for watching! I hope you enjoyed this deep dive into organizing your POMs in CLO. If you have any questions, the comment section down below is for you to ask, and one of us will get back to you. If you liked this video, please like and subscribe. Don't forget to check out all the videos on the CLO channel because there's so much great information available, all completely free. Thanks again for watching! ```
